report.summary: The release changes how console logs are formatted, configured, and written, which may affect their appearance and handling.
keyChanges: Error entries now pass their error status under a different name than the writer reads, so routing them to the error output may no longer work.
The fancy reporter still clears the console when requested, but its clear operation now calls a writer that requires options, risking an exception before the log appears.
Write mode now uses string values such as "async"; callers that previously supplied boolean true may no longer get asynchronous completion.
Reporter options are now merged at the top level, so custom streams and formatting settings can take effect instead of being nested under an options property.

Log writing now selects the configured error stream for error output and uses a shared stream-writing path; formatting and tag preparation have also been replaced, so their exact output needs confirmation.
Background-color formatting now accepts hex values beginning with # and named colors; repeated lookups use a cache, so verify they continue to return a usable color.
Console output writing now has default, asynchronous drain-waiting, and synchronous modes, and the reporter passes its selected output stream and mode.
Message formatting now translates named placeholders such as %message$s into positional format arguments.
The fancy reporter now honors icons supplied in its options; for a log entry with no explicit icon, it now displays the default ❯ icon instead of suppressing the icon.
qaChecks: Verify an error entry with its error status set to true is sent to the error output rather than the regular output.
Check a fancy log entry with clearing enabled clears the console and then prints its message without an exception.
Confirm a log requested with the legacy asynchronous value true waits for the stream's drain signal before completion.
Verify that a normal log with the message “custom-output-check” is written to the configured custom output stream.
Check that a sync error log and an async error log containing “error-route-check” are written to the configured error stream, not the normal output stream.
Confirm that a log with the tag “service:cache” and message “tag-check” is emitted with its date, type, tag, and message represented in the formatted output.
Verify a message format containing %message$s and arguments in date, type, tag, message order displays the supplied message in the formatted output.
Check asynchronous output when the stream refuses a write temporarily: it should complete only after the stream emits drain.
Confirm requesting the same named or #-prefixed background color twice produces usable color formatting both times.
Verify a log entry of type log with no explicit icon displays ❯.
Check that a custom icon supplied in the reporter options appears on an entry of the matching type.
Verify an extension that imports the reporter’s built-in icon list still loads; before this release the list was available, so confirm its removal is intended.
Verify a red badge in the fancy console output; before this release its badge background was red, so confirm the new coloring is intended.

Check a custom output format set to the exact built-in object-property label used for string conversion: before this release it was processed as ordinary input, and now it may be treated as a cached entry; confirm the new result is intended.
Verify a message with the type “log” and no custom icon; before this release it appeared without an icon, so confirm that the default icon appearing now is intended.
Verify colored output that uses the same background color twice: before this release both uses returned the color formatter, and now the second may fail; confirm the new result is intended.
Verify an asynchronous write to a slow output that returns false: before this release the call returned immediately, and now it waits for the drain event; confirm the wait is intended.
Check a console entry configured with the exact color #ff0000; before this release it was treated as a named color, so confirm that it now appears in hexadecimal red as intended.
Verify a custom console format containing %message$s; before this release the named placeholder was not converted for substitution, so confirm that the message now appears in its place as intended.
Verify a basic message with the default reporter settings; before this release the line could show “4$s” instead of the message, and confirm the new message formatting is intended.
Verify in the asynchronous logging setup that, when output is backpressured, a message waits for the stream to drain as it did before this release, and confirm the new result is intended.
Check the console output for an error message and verify that it still goes to the error output stream as it did before this release, or confirm that sending it to regular output is intended.

Verify an error message with synchronous logging enabled and separate regular and error streams; before this release it went to the regular output stream, and confirm it now goes to the error stream as intended.
Check a log entry using a custom format containing %message$s; before this release the message was not substituted for that named placeholder, so confirm the new displayed result is intended.
Check a reporter configured with a custom output stream; before this release its messages went to the default stream, and confirm they now go to the custom stream.
Check successful messages after setting a custom icon; before this release the built-in success icon appeared, so confirm that the custom icon appearing now is intended.
uncertainty: The previous asynchronous writer selection is not supplied, so confirm whether callers passed boolean true and expected completion to wait for the stream to drain.

The replacement formatting path is not fully shown, so it is unclear whether colon-separated tags such as “service:cache” still appear as “service - cache” or whether the previous tag formatting rule has changed.

The supplied changes contain no prior implementation for comparison, so no concrete input that the old behavior handled differently can be established; application navigation and user-facing surfaces are also not provided.
The formerly exported icon map is no longer exported; the supplied evidence does not establish whether package consumers rely on that export or how to test compatibility.

report.summary: The release makes drawing edits more capable and reliable, with improved controls, guidance, and undo history.
keyChanges: You can now drag line and arrow points directly, add a point with Alt-click, and close a path by dragging an endpoint near the other endpoint; point placement accounts for rotation and overlapping handles favor the last-rendered point.
Point updates with the same number of points are now skipped when the comparison finds no change, which may overlook an update limited to the first point.

Double-clicking or pressing Enter with exactly one line, arrow, or freehand stroke selected now enters point editing instead of the previous double-click text-editing path; the canvas shows handles for that element.

While point editing is active, pointer actions can interact with the points, and editing is finalized when its element is no longer selected; point-editing state is initialized as inactive and excluded from locally saved editor state.
The drawing renderer now displays point handles during editing and suppresses the usual selection overlay, so verify both on-canvas appearance and exported output.
Entering line or arrow point editing now shifts the first point to [0,0] and adjusts the element position; point handles are calculated using the element’s rotation for drawing and hit detection.

While editing a line or arrow, Alt-click adds a point, Alt-drag updates an uncommitted endpoint, and releasing Alt removes that uncommitted point; dragging an endpoint of a closed path into the loop threshold snaps it to the other endpoint.
Resize-handle hit detection now receives the pointer’s scene x and y as separate coordinates, so selected-element resizing and rotation should remain usable at different canvas positions.
Selecting one line or arrow now shows context-sensitive guidance for editing it, including whether an editing point is selected; the guidance also formats shortcut names for the user’s platform.
Undo history now stores the line or arrow being edited and distinguishes changes to the editing target, while changes within the same target do not alone create another history entry.

Shortcut-name substitutions now apply to whole tokens rather than matching those letters inside longer words. The supplied evidence does not show a user-facing shortcut containing such an embedded token.
Editing a line or arrow now uses bounds derived from its generated curve to keep the element’s position aligned as its points change.
Scene elements can now be looked up by ID, with a separate lookup that excludes deleted elements; the supplied evidence does not establish a distinct visible workflow change.

Deleting an active point now removes that point rather than deleting the whole selected drawing element; deleting when only one point remains removes the element, and group editing selects a remaining sibling when available.

Finishing while editing a line or arrow now exits point editing, keeps a visible element with at least two points, and removes an element with fewer than two points or one too small to see; Escape is also newly accepted when point editing and a drag are active together.
qaChecks: Verify that Alt-clicking a rotated line adds a point at the pointer location, and that Alt-moving the pointer updates the new point with the line’s rotation applied.

Check that dragging a line point changes its visible position while the other points remain in place; for an equal-length point update where only the first point changes, confirm that the first point’s visible position updates.
Confirm that dragging a line’s start or end point near the opposite endpoint closes the path and leaves the endpoints joined after pointer release.
Verify that double-clicking the selected line or arrow enters point editing and shows handles instead of starting text editing; repeat by pressing Enter with the element selected.
Check that dragging a visible point changes the line or arrow, and that clicking within the element to add a point leaves the drawing editable.
Confirm that deselecting the element exits point editing and that the selection can be made again without stale point-editing handles.
Verify that exporting while point editing is active includes the drawing but not the red-and-white point-editing handles.
Verify that entering point editing for a line or arrow with a nonzero first-point offset shows handles at the visible points and that selecting a handle selects the element.
Check that Alt-clicking the line at a new location adds a point, then moving the pointer with Alt held updates the uncommitted endpoint and releasing Alt removes that uncommitted endpoint.
Test dragging an endpoint of a closed path to within the loop-closing threshold and releasing; confirm the endpoint snaps to the other endpoint.
Confirm that dragging a point on a rotated line and dragging a selected shape’s resize or rotation handle responds at the pointer location.
Verify that selecting one line or arrow outside point editing displays its line-editing guidance, and that entering point editing displays guidance for the editing state.
Check the first point specifically: with point index 0 selected, confirm whether the hint says a point is selected rather than indicating that nothing is selected.
Test entering edit mode on the first line and then switching the editing target to the second; Undo should restore the first editing target, and Redo should restore the second.
Verify that changing the selected editing point on the same line does not by itself add an undo step, while an actual drawing change can still be undone.
Verify dragging the line’s first point moves that point while the remaining path stays in place and the drawing remains correctly positioned.
Verify that deleting an active point from a two-point line or arrow leaves the element with one point instead of deleting the whole element.
Check deletion again with that one-point element active; the element should be removed, point editing should end, and any remaining group sibling should become selected when editing a group.
Confirm that Escape while editing a visible line or arrow with at least two points ends point editing and keeps the element; with only one point remaining, Escape should remove it.
Test Escape while point editing and a drag are active at the same time, with no multi-point drawing in progress; Escape should now finish point editing.
Verify that moving or deleting the first point of a rotated line or arrow leaves its other points in place; before this release the remaining shape could shift, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify on the canvas that pressing Delete with the middle point active on a selected three-point line used to remove the whole line, and confirm that removing just that point is intended.
Verify that you enter point-editing mode and move the pointer over different points; before this release, the active-point indication did not follow the pointer, and confirm it now does.

Verify that you enter point-editing mode on a line or arrow with several points; before this release, no point handles appeared, and confirm the handles and active-point highlight now appear as intended.
Verify that you enter point-editing mode on a line or arrow and click between two points; before this release, the click did not add a point there, and confirm the new point is added as intended.

Check a one-point line by changing the coordinates of its sole point without adding or removing points; before this release the point changed, but now it stays put, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that clicking overlapping control points selects the one drawn on top; before this release an underlying point could be selected instead, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that you select exactly one line or arrow and double-click the canvas; before this release, the double-click could start text editing, and confirm it now enters point editing.

Verify in the canvas that moving a control point on a curved, rough line keeps the line positioned using its rendered curve bounds; before this release those bounds were not used, so confirm the new positioning is intended.
Verify that clicking Done while editing a one-point line used to leave the line on the canvas, and confirm that removing it now is intended.
Verify that Alt-clicking a rotated line or arrow adds a point at the clicked location; before this release the point could appear in the wrong place, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify while editing a group that pressing Delete on the only point of a line that is not selected as a whole used to leave the line and selection unchanged, and confirm that removing it and selecting another group element is intended.
Verify that while editing a line or arrow, dragging a visible control point moves it; before this release it did not move through this drag path, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify after replacing a drawing with a new list that reuses an existing element ID but changes its content, lookups return the updated element; before this release the scene did not maintain an ID index, so confirm this new lookup behavior is intended.
Verify that you enter point-editing mode on a selected line or arrow; before this release, its usual selection overlay was drawn, and confirm that it is now suppressed as intended.
uncertainty: Updates that change only the first point in an equal-length point list may be skipped; the evidence does not establish whether a normal canvas action produces this input, so confirm first-point editing carefully.

The renderer draws point handles for the active element, and the export renderer uses that renderer; it is unclear whether exporting during point editing is intended to include those handles, making this the main output risk to resolve.

Before-change implementations are not supplied for the new line-editing methods, so the exact user input that was handled differently before and after cannot be established; these checks verify the supplied behavior but do not confirm a regression against the prior version.

The new hint checks the selected point index by truthiness, so index 0 is treated as no point selected; confirm whether this is intended. The shortcut-formatting difference is concrete for a value such as AltGraph on Mac, but no supplied user-facing shortcut value contains that embedded token, so this edge case has no identified app navigation for manual verification.

The new curve-bounds and scene-lookup code has no removed implementation to compare, so the supplied evidence does not identify a concrete input that behaved differently before this change. Navigation details were also not supplied.

The supplied context gives no navigation path, and does not establish whether the editor allows a drag to be active while a line or arrow is being point-edited, so the newly accepted Escape condition may need a suitable manual setup.

report.summary: The release overhauls how the editor and showcase app start, share, and manage collaborative drawing sessions.
keyChanges: Live collaboration now encrypts scene and participant updates for sharing, while recognizing room links only when the URL hash exactly matches #room=ID,key, with letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens in each value.
Scene restoration now accepts missing data and returns restored empty elements and default settings instead of requiring a data object.
The supplied changes remove the prior collaboration reconciliation and room-dialog implementations; replacement behavior is not shown, so their user-visible effect cannot be confirmed.
Scene startup now waits for supplied initial data and restores a blank scene if that promise rejects; verify startup completes rather than remaining stuck loading.
The embeddable editor now exposes a readiness promise and expanded drawing controls, defaults omitted dimensions to the browser window, and allows scene updates without supplying elements.
Collaboration scene updates now flow through the editor change callback, and pointer updates are passed to the collaboration wrapper instead of being sent directly from the editor.

External drawings are now recognized from a nonempty id query, a strictly formatted encrypted drawing hash, or a collaboration link; loading a link can prompt before replacing a saved drawing, except when the local drawing is empty or the same collaboration room was recently left.
Drawing edits are saved locally and broadcast to collaborators; the previous explicit saving of a changed collaboration username has been removed.
Returning to the same collaboration room within 15 seconds can bypass the saved-drawing override prompt when the recent-room marker is present.

The desktop and mobile canvas menus replace the embedded room dialog with a collaboration button; the button appears only when a click handler is provided, and its participant count is shown only when the count is above zero.
Live cursor updates no longer include the sender’s selected-element IDs, although they still include pointer, button, and username details.

Editor-side collaboration setup, remote drawing updates, session shutdown, and save-before-leaving handling were removed here; verify that collaboration still creates and synchronizes rooms, safely handles deleted drawing content, and preserves unsaved edits.
The embeddable editor contract now accepts null or promise-based initial data and exposes a readiness promise, allowing integrations to wait for initialization.

When two collaborators have the same drawing element at the same version but different conflict markers, the merge now keeps a winning copy instead of potentially omitting the element when the remote marker wins.

Collaboration sync now supplies the scene elements to be sent at each broadcast, including full scene updates for new participants; leaving an unsaved collaborative session also attempts to save it and may prompt before navigation.

Live collaboration now sends selected-element information from the editor state when available, and sends an empty selection when that state is unavailable; collaborators may therefore see different selection information in that edge case.
The embeddable editor now forwards collaboration-status and pointer-update inputs and uses a revised editor-reference input, while no longer forwarding the previous username-change input.
Live collaboration synchronizes drawing changes and participant presence; remote drawing updates clear the local undo history.
The collaboration dialog supports starting or ending a session, copying its link, and changing the participant name.
A new session clears drawing history before sharing, and drawing updates are broadcast only when the scene version is newer than the last received or sent version.

uncertainty: The prior collaboration conflict-resolution rules and room-dialog close behavior were removed, but replacement code and navigation details were not supplied; it is unclear whether these behaviors remain available or how a conflicting edit should now resolve.

The editor now passes pointer updates during two-pointer gestures, whereas the previous direct broadcast skipped them; the supplied evidence does not show how the collaboration wrapper handles those updates, so check for confusing remote pointer behavior.
The previous handler that saved a changed collaboration username was removed, but the supplied changes do not establish whether another path now preserves it.

The supplied evidence removes prior scene-loading, collaboration-saving, full-scene-broadcast, and event-teardown logic but does not show replacement behavior; in particular, it does not establish what should happen for an empty scene or when reopening the same room within 15 seconds.

The prior collaboration setup, remote-update, and unload-save code is removed from the editor in this group, but this evidence does not show whether replacement handling preserves those behaviors; the deleted-content and unsaved-edit checks are especially important.

The protection for locally edited, resized, or dragged elements now reads the collaboration wrapper's stored editor state rather than the editor state directly; verify that this stored state is current when remote updates arrive during an interaction.

The supplied evidence does not establish whether integrations rely on the removed username-change input or how they should migrate, and it does not show how to produce the missing-editor-state case through normal user actions.
The supplied changes contain no removed code, so the prior behavior is unavailable and no concrete input handled differently before and after this change can be established.

report.summary: The release standardizes how canvas positioning and viewport offsets are handled when editing, loading, importing, and exporting drawings.
keyChanges: Canvas-to-drawing position mapping now accounts for horizontal and vertical offsets as well as zoom, affecting pointer interactions, pasted content, and scene positioning; checks should focus on offset canvases, where the old mapping ignored those offsets.
Text editing and text placement now use the same offset-aware positioning, so text should remain aligned with its drawing element while editing or snapping to an element’s center.
The editor now measures and applies its canvas position, updating it when the editor size changes; imported scene state also preserves the editor’s current dimensions and position.

Loading a scene or dropping an Excalidraw file now recalculates the view around its drawing content, instead of relying solely on the saved scroll position; restoration no longer has its former optional scroll-to-content behavior.
Loading a drawing file now uses the current editor view to calculate where its elements are positioned, so verify imports with content outside the current view.
Shared-drawing imports no longer request automatic scrolling to the drawing content, so verify that imported elements remain visible and reachable.
Browser-stored and exported drawing state omits the top and left viewport offsets, even when they have nonzero values.
Node canvas export now starts with both viewport offsets set to zero. The added state fields do not otherwise change runtime behavior.
qaChecks: Verify that clicking the shape to add or edit text positions the text over the intended drawing location, and that text snapped to the shape center remains centered.
Check that text stays aligned with its element while editing at these offsets and zoom, and that submitted text remains in the drawing.
Test pasting a copied drawing element at a canvas point with these offsets and zoom; confirm the pasted element appears at the pointer location rather than shifted.
Verify that loading the drawing file with its saved view away from its elements brings the drawing content into view using the current editor viewport.
Check that opening a saved scene link with nonempty content and a saved view away from the content brings the drawing into view rather than retaining that saved scroll position.
Confirm that the canvas remains aligned with its editor container after the editor dimensions change, including when the container is offset from the page origin.
Verify importing the file while the editor is showing a different view positions the drawing using the current editor view, with its elements centered in view.
Confirm the shared drawing loads and its elements remain visible and reachable even though restoration no longer requests automatic scrolling to the content.
Verify the drawing saves to browser storage and exports without retaining either nonzero offset.
Confirm the canvas export renders the drawing with both viewport offsets set to zero.
Confirm that dropping an Excalidraw file with artwork outside the current view previously scrolled to its content, and verify that the new positioning based on the current canvas is intended.

Verify opening a scene whose saved view leaves its drawing off-screen; before this release it kept that saved view, and now the drawing is repositioned using its contents and the canvas position, so confirm this is intended.

Verify drawing in an app embedded in a container positioned away from the page’s top-left corner; before this release drawing used no measured host offset, and now it uses the container’s position, so confirm pointer placement is intended.

Verify an embedded app in a page container offset from the top-left corner and with constrained dimensions; before this release the app container had no explicit size or position, and now it receives both, so confirm its placement and size are intended.

Check that clicking or pasting at a location in a zoomed canvas offset from the page origin previously mapped to scene coordinates without accounting for those offsets, and confirm the new placement is intended.
Verify that a scene position displayed in a zoomed canvas offset from the page origin was previously calculated without those offsets, and confirm its new viewport position is intended.

Confirm that, when editing text at a zoom other than 100% in a canvas offset from the page origin, the editor previously used a zoom transform that ignored those offsets and that the new alignment is intended.
Check editing existing text in a zoomed canvas positioned away from the page origin; before, its position was calculated without the canvas offsets, so confirm the new positioning is intended.
Check a Node PNG export of a drawing with elements away from the origin; before this release, the render had no top or left offsets, and confirm the elements now appear in the intended positions.

Verify undoing or redoing after resizing or moving an embedded app; before this release applying the history result could restore stale dimensions and did not preserve the current host position, and now those current values are retained, so confirm this is intended.
Verify that opening a shared scene whose saved view does not show its artwork previously scrolled to the content, and confirm that retaining the imported view without automatic scrolling is intended.

Verify opening a scene link in an embedded app whose container is offset from the page’s top-left corner; before this release the scene initialized before that position was measured, and now it is measured first, so confirm the new placement is intended.

Verify restoring a drawing with a request to bring its content into view; before this release that request centered the drawing, and now the saved scroll position is retained, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that starting text editing at a zoom other than 100% in a canvas offset from the page origin previously created an editor whose transform did not account for those offsets, and confirm the new alignment is intended.

Verify that clicking near the center of a shape in an offset, zoomed canvas and typing text previously used a center position calculated without the canvas offsets, and confirm the new center placement is intended.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not explain how to create the specified canvas offsets through the application, so the host layout or test setup may need to provide them.

report.summary: Editing lines and arrows in the drawing editor now provides clearer, more consistent point selection and control.
keyChanges: A selected, unlocked line or arrow now shows editable point handles when it is the only selected element and its point-editing state matches; editing handles are larger and use purple styling.

Lines and arrows now omit side and rotation transform handles, while the new default selection state starts empty; a horizontal two-point line is a useful boundary case because the previous handle logic treated its zero vertical point coordinate specially.
A hovered line or arrow point now receives a highlight; the highlight is drawn outside the selection-rendering guard, so its appearance in image exports needs confirmation.
Selecting one line or arrow, including through the canvas context-menu interaction, now keeps its point editor in sync with selection so its points can be hovered, dragged, and bound to shapes.

For a selected line or arrow, pointer targeting now follows the actual line geometry instead of treating its entire bounding box as a hit; point-editor state is also cleared when that element is no longer selected.
Selecting exactly one line or arrow with Select All, or finishing a multipoint drawing, now activates its point editor so individual points can be selected and dragged.
Locking a selected line or arrow clears its point editor; point handles are now 10 pixels instead of 20, while the hit-test threshold remains 11 pixels.

report.summary: The release improves how line and arrow editing handles points, curves, and segment controls.
keyChanges: While editing a multi-point line or arrow, the editor now shows a handle for each eligible segment midpoint and inserts a new point into the segment whose midpoint is clicked; rounded lines use the curve midpoint.
A segment shorter on screen than four point-handle sizes has no midpoint handle, and multi-point lines show these handles only while being edited; two-point lines retain a midpoint handle.
During rendering, editing handles are taken from the visible version of the selected line or arrow, addressing mismatches during live collaboration.

For rounded lines with more than two points, midpoint placement is calculated along the curve’s sampled length, so a segment’s midpoint handle can differ from the straight-line midpoint between its endpoints.
Curve length and sampled points now support midpoint placement and the existing short-segment and handle logic; point matching uses exact equality of both coordinates.

Previously, midpoint editing was unavailable on lines and arrows with three or more points; the editor now tracks midpoint hover by segment, so verify that a multi-segment line or arrow offers editable segment midpoints.
Pointer movement now handles the absence of an active line or arrow editor by returning without editing; normal canvas pointer use should remain unaffected when no line or arrow is being edited.
qaChecks: Verify that, while editing a three-point line, midpoint handles appear on eligible segments; click the midpoint of the second segment and confirm a new point is inserted into that segment while existing points remain.

Check a three-point rounded line by hovering over and clicking a displayed segment midpoint; confirm the hover highlight follows the pointer and the new point is inserted on the curve within the selected segment.
Confirm that a segment shorter on screen than four point-handle sizes has no midpoint handle, while a two-point line still has a midpoint handle and supports adding a point.
Verify in a live collaboration session that after one participant edits a line, the other participant sees its editing handles aligned with the synchronized line.

report.summary: The release reorganizes editor footers and changes how embedded editors display custom content and a sign-in-gated link.
keyChanges: The mobile footer no longer receives its previous language selector; verify the footer on a phone-sized screen.
Custom footer content previously supplied by an embedding application is no longer passed into the editor footer, while the Excalidraw.com app now places its own footer content inside the editor.
Custom footer content previously supplied through the footer callback is now supplied as a child in the centered desktop footer; the mobile menu no longer renders the former callback content.
A link to Excalidraw+ is now shown only to signed-in Excalidraw+ users and opens in a new tab.
Embedded editors now provide footer content as children instead of through the former footer-rendering option, with that content placed in the centered footer area.
The example embed retains its comment-tool control and adds another footer control; the Excalidraw+ link is shown when the browser cookie string contains the authentication-state cookie name.
Child content supplied by an embedding host is now passed into the editor, so integrations can display content within it.
The editor no longer forwards the former custom-footer option; the package also newly exposes a Footer component for integrations.

report.summary: The release standardizes how drawing tools access selected objects, with no confirmed change to what users see.
keyChanges: Canvas selection is now read through a shared scene-level selector, including during pointer, keyboard, text-editing, context-menu, and color-picker interactions; grouping, alignment, distribution, flipping, and frame membership also use this selection path.

Some selection lookups now use the current non-deleted drawing by default, while frame and group operations can still supply their own element lists. The supplied evidence does not establish a normal user-visible change in results.
Library addition now reads the selected objects through the editor’s scene, including attached text and frame contents; the supplied code shows no intended change to what is added.
Selection, duplication, and horizontal or vertical flipping now pass editor context into group or frame handling; no change to the expected visible results is established.
The editor clears scene and selection caches when it is removed, and selection lookup now maintains a cache; no user-visible effect is specified.

Both zoom-to-fit selection actions and context-sensitive editing hints now obtain selected elements from the editor’s scene rather than from a supplied element list; their visible result depends on the scene’s current selection.
Editor action panels now receive the editor instance, supporting the updated scene-based selection lookup.
Selection-based keyboard actions, line editing, and context-menu labels now read selected elements through the editor’s scene, while retaining the specified bound-text and frame-selection options.
Paste, library insertion, and drop flows now pass the editor instance into their shared insertion process, but the supplied evidence does not establish a changed visible result.
All six alignment controls now use the editor’s current selection to decide whether they are available; alignment still requires more than one selected object and excludes frames.
Locking, its context-menu wording, and its keyboard shortcut now also query the editor’s current selection; applying the lock still includes attached text and objects inside frames.
The six alignment actions still line selected elements up by left, right, top, bottom, or horizontal or vertical center, while selection and frame-membership handling now use the current scene.

report.summary: The release improves how users find and use editor commands, drawing tools, sharing options, and dialogs.
keyChanges: Shortcut lookup now supports a requested alternate shortcut, falling back to the first shortcut when that position is unavailable; the command-palette shortcut hint can therefore show the alternate choice.
The command palette now supports keyboard selection and command execution; executing a command closes the palette and clears its search.
Dialog focus is deferred until after the dialog appears, and the dedicated close button is now shown only in fullscreen mobile dialogs, not desktop dialogs.
The command palette can now be opened from a new editor menu item, its shortcut is listed in Help, and Ctrl/Cmd+P now shows a shortcut hint instead of continuing as a normal keypress.
Double-clicking a selected line or arrow that is already being edited no longer exits early, so verify the canvas interaction still behaves as intended.
Canvas context-menu labels are now read from the item label rather than the previous context-specific label field; items using only the old field may appear without a label.
Links now open with opener access disabled, and dialogs apply the animations-disabled setting that is present when the dialog is created.
The new command palette gathers drawing, editor, tool, export, library, and color-change commands, and supports searching and running available commands.
The palette can be opened or closed with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P or Ctrl/Cmd+/.

The editor command palette now includes sharing and live-collaboration actions, social links, and Excalidraw+ sign-up, account, and export actions; the account-related choices differ for signed-in and signed-out users.
The share dialog closes when an editor dialog is opened, preventing both dialogs from remaining open together.

Element-lock actions now show selection-specific labels and icons; with no selection the toggle is unavailable, and the unlock-all action is available only when nothing is selected and at least one element is locked.
The recovery screen’s GitHub issue action continues to open a new tab and now prevents that tab from accessing the editor tab through its opener.
Canvas, alignment, and link actions now provide labels and icons for editor controls; the theme action also has searchable theme-related terms and an icon and label that reflect the current theme.
In the command palette, activating the image command by keyboard requests direct-on-canvas insertion, while activating it by mouse selects the image tool without that option.
Frame, grouping, and history actions now provide labels and icons through the shared action registration; the frame tool is explicitly unavailable in view mode.
Line editing is categorized under elements for the command palette, and its action label now safely handles a missing selection.
Editor actions now carry labels and icons, and stats, view mode, and zen mode have command-palette names; verify these commands can be found and identified in the searchable command list.
The objects snap mode action changes from marked for view mode to not marked for view mode, so its availability while view mode is active needs confirmation.

New shortcut mappings cover opening the command palette, zoom controls, selection fitting, tools, saving, and shortcut help; verify the mappings, including both command-palette shortcuts, are recognized or shown where applicable.
Dropdown menus now remove their Escape-key listener using the same capture setting used to add it, preventing stale listeners after menus close.

Action definitions now use the general action label field instead of the context-menu-specific field, and many also supply icons; verify action names and icons are presented correctly across selection, editing, library, and collaboration controls.

Copy-as-SVG, copy-as-PNG, and copy-text actions now include clipboard and format keywords, while export, save, load, and export-option actions receive labels and icons; verify these controls are identified correctly.

Verify that pressing Down Arrow in a newly opened, empty palette selects the command you last ran; before this release it moved into the regular list, so confirm the new navigation order is intended.

Verify in view-only mode that clicking an unavailable command does nothing; before this release the entry was not treated as disabled, so confirm the new non-interactive result is intended.

Verify that in an editable drawing, searching the command palette for “Clear canvas” now offers the clear-canvas command; before this release it was not offered, so confirm this new result is intended.
Confirm that pressing Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows or Linux, or Cmd+Shift+P on Mac, opens the command palette; before this release those keys did not open it, and verify the new shortcut is intended.

Check that with only an image selected, searching the command palette for a stroke-color command does not show one; before this release the palette had no stroke-color command, so confirm this selection-dependent result is intended.
Verify that a Ctrl+Shift+P hint appears as three separate keycaps; before this release it appeared as one combined hint, so confirm the separated display is intended.
Check the command palette with a selection that changes an action's palette entry; before this release the entry used the action's unadjusted details, so confirm the customized result is intended.

Verify that deleting a selected object from the palette happens after the palette closes; before this release the canvas change could overlap the closing transition, so confirm the new sequence is intended.

Check that a custom command with an unrecognized category and no specified order appears after the built-in categories; before this release the palette did not apply category ordering, so confirm this placement is intended.
Verify in the canvas action menu that searching for “svg” now finds the SVG copy action, which previously had no SVG search keyword, and confirm this new result and its icon are intended.
Verify after selecting an element that searching the action menu for “opacity” finds the opacity action, which previously had no general action-menu label, and confirm this new result is intended.
uncertainty: Most command-palette handlers are supplied only as additions, so their prior behavior and a regression-specific input for those behaviors cannot be established from this evidence.
The supplied evidence does not show whether context-menu item providers have been updated to the new label field, so items still using only the previous field may lose their displayed labels.
Before versions were not supplied for the newly added palette behavior, so no concrete input that changed from working before to behaving differently now can be established.
No affected application areas or navigation steps were supplied, so the exact menus or controls where these action labels and icons appear could not be identified.
The supplied evidence does not define what the view-mode setting means for action availability, so confirm whether objects snap mode is intended to be available while view mode is active.

The supplied evidence changes action metadata but does not establish which application surfaces display it or provide a before-and-after user input that behaves differently; navigation was not supplied, so confirm the updated names and icons appear in the relevant controls.

report.summary: The release adds support for creating, editing, routing, and restoring elbow arrows while keeping connected shapes and drawings in sync.
keyChanges: Elbow arrows now calculate routes around shapes and simplify straight runs; connector paths and bends may change as they are drawn or edited.
Binding points and direction selection now account for rotated shape bounds and use adaptive midpoint snapping, affecting where connectors attach, including on diamonds.
Connector routes are recalculated during drawing and when bound shapes or arrow points are edited, resized, rotated, or flipped.
Elbow-arrow bends now render as rounded corners with a maximum radius of 16 pixels, reduced to no more than half the length of either adjoining segment.
While dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint, shape detection can include the shape’s interior bounds, and arrow connections are recalculated as elements move or change.
New elbow-arrow routing calculates paths around drawing elements, so connectors may take different bent routes as diagrams are edited.
Undo and redo now include the drawing when recalculating bound arrows, and newly initialized editor state sets the arrow type to round.
Arrow controls now support sharp, rounded, and elbow styles; roundness controls are no longer available for arrows, and elbow arrows do not show the line-point editor.
Elbow arrows route around shapes and keep their endpoints connected as shapes move; editing is focused on endpoints, and a bound elbow arrow cannot be resized or dragged by itself.
The arrow tool now shows its own editing hint, and pressing A while using the arrow tool cycles through sharp, rounded, and elbow styles.
Elbow arrows now use fixed attachment points so their connections can follow changes to connected shapes; duplicating an arrow also preserves its binding details.
Elbow arrows no longer show rotation or bounding-box handles, and their point handles and highlights are limited to the supported editing affordances.
Negative angles are now converted to a non-negative degree value by adding 360 degrees once, so an angle of -90 degrees is represented as 270 degrees.
The Stats panel no longer offers angle editing for elbow arrows; changing size or position through the panel now also supplies drawing context for updating connected arrows and attached text.
Restoring a drawing now preserves an arrow’s elbow-routing flag and repairs elbow-arrow bindings that lack a fixed-point anchor by using [0, 0], while clearing fixed-point data on non-elbow bindings.
Arrow data converted into drawing elements now uses the arrow-specific creation path, and selection actions can distinguish the arrow tool from other tools.

Arrow appearance controls now offer sharp, round, and elbow styles; converting an arrow to elbow style can connect its endpoints to shapes and route around them, while changing away from elbow style keeps only the endpoints.
Elbow arrows are excluded from the line editor and do not gain midpoint handles; their point changes use routed-arrow behavior, and edge-roundness changes no longer apply to them.
Arrow connections are updated during drawing, point editing, and canvas or Stats panel transforms, including flips, moves, and resizes; bound elbow arrows also use fixed attachment points.
Alt-clicking an edited non-elbow line now adds a point even when it already has an uncommitted point; previously that case did not add one.
Elbow arrows now follow pointer movement without grid snapping and finalize after their start and end points, so drawing and editing should preserve the intended two-ended bent connector.
Changing or deleting a shape connected to an elbow arrow now recalculates the connector route, and undo or redo applies those connection updates through the drawing history.
Ordinary lines continue to be created without arrowheads; chart-generation changes leave their existing plain-line appearance unchanged.

report.summary: The release expands the editor’s lasso selection tools and interactions, including how selections and drawing feedback behave.
keyChanges: Lasso selection now uses sampled outlines for curves, rounded shapes, and ellipses instead of the previous point-based paths and ellipse cross-lines, which can change which objects a lasso selects.

Lasso-selected bound text now selects its container, selected frames exclude their children from the selection, and a single selected line or arrow enters point-editing mode. Geometry updates also feed frame membership, drawing selection, and rendering.
Lasso strokes now use an animated dashed outline and clear when the gesture ends; short strokes may show little or no outline.
Updating or ending a laser-pointer stroke now clears retained trails, so released strokes should no longer linger; check local and collaborator pointers.
Choosing the lasso tool can now preserve the existing selection when requested, while the default remains to clear it.
New shapes are no longer resized from their center, even when the center-resize modifier is held; they remain anchored at the initial pointer position.
Lasso gestures now select drawing elements as the pointer moves, display a temporary trail, and clear that trail and its tracking state when the gesture ends.
Holding Alt while dragging a selection rectangle switches to lasso selection; releasing Alt during that gesture returns to rectangle selection.
Starting a lasso normally clears the current selection, while Shift preserves it; lasso selection is also no longer cleared by canvas interaction.
Restoration now accepts “lasso” as a recognized tool, so a drawing restored with that tool active should retain it.

Line-segment intersection calculations can now use an explicitly supplied distance tolerance; callers that omit it keep the previous default, so existing lasso-selection and arrow-binding behavior is not shown to change.

The toolbar now offers lasso mode, and the command palette includes a command to toggle it; clicking the selection control while selection mode is already active now switches to lasso instead of leaving selection mode active.
With lasso active and nothing selected, selection-property actions are hidden; releasing Space in lasso mode resets the cursor instead of following the other-tool path that clears selection.
A new lasso tool selects drawing elements enclosed by or intersected by a drawn loop; turning it on clears the current selection, and turning it off returns to the selection tool.

Separate alternate action names were removed for canvas background, clearing the canvas, the hand tool, unlocking elements, stats, view mode, and zen mode; the supplied context does not establish how this affects action discovery.

Verify that a lasso path passing just under one pixel from a shape’s outline now selects it; before this release the near miss did not count as an intersection, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify in the toolbar with the embed tool selected that its icon now has a thicker stroke; before this release it was thinner, so confirm the new appearance is intended.
uncertainty: The lasso routines and selection normalization are newly added without removed-code evidence for their previous behavior, so the intended outcomes for bound text, frame children, and line point-editing cannot be compared with a documented prior rule.
The exact key or modifier that previously enabled center-based shape drawing is not established by the supplied evidence; use the editor’s existing center-resize modifier if known.

No current application caller supplies the new intersection tolerance, and no user-facing route for exercising a custom tolerance is supplied; therefore an exact user input that changes intersection results cannot be identified from this evidence.
The supplied evidence confirms lasso can be activated but does not establish how canvas gestures select elements, so the expected result of lassoing elements remains unresolved.
The supplied context does not identify an action-discovery surface, so it is unclear whether removing the alternate action names affects how users find those actions.

report.summary: The release streamlines how users create, place, and navigate flowcharts in the editor.
keyChanges: Keyboard shortcuts for creating and navigating flowcharts now use shared handling that commits created nodes on modifier release and selects and reveals the created or navigated-to node when needed.
Creating flowchart nodes now looks for space around already connected nodes instead of using the former fixed, centered layout, so generated nodes may shift to avoid overlap.
Repeated creation in the same direction keeps the cluster aligned where space permits, while changing direction or ending creation clears that placement state.
Directional navigation now finds linked nodes using elbow arrows and the arrow’s position relative to the current node.
Newly created flowchart nodes are placed in a cluster one 100-pixel gap from the parent, with the cluster shifted to the nearest available cross-axis space to avoid nodes in the connected flowchart.

When a pending cluster grows, its existing nodes are intended to keep their positions if the enlarged cluster still fits; the previous rightward default and unknown-key fallback are no longer shown in the supplied implementation evidence.
Flowchart creation state and pending nodes are now accessed through a dedicated editor controller; the supplied evidence does not show a change to creation, navigation, or undo and redo behavior.
qaChecks: Verify holding Ctrl or Command and pressing an arrow key from a selected flowchart node previews a connected node in that direction, then releasing the modifier commits it and selects the first created node.
Check that pressing Escape while flowchart creation is in progress cancels the pending creation.
Confirm Alt plus an arrow key from a selected node selects the node in that direction, and releasing Alt ends navigation.

Verify that pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Right on the selected flowchart shape creates a connected node to the right and places it in a clear neighboring slot rather than overlapping the connected shape in the intended slot.

Check that creating a second node with Ctrl/Cmd+Right keeps the same-direction additions grouped where space permits, and that starting creation in a different direction resets the previous placement.
Confirm that Alt+Arrow navigation from a shape follows an elbow-arrow connection in the chosen direction to the linked shape.

Verify that adding a node where the parent-centered placement would meet that branch puts the new node in the nearest clear cross-axis space, without overlap and with the 100-pixel primary-axis gap from its parent.

Check that growing a pending cluster by one node keeps the already visible pending nodes in place when the enlarged cluster still fits; add an obstacle that prevents the anchored placement and confirm the cluster moves to available space instead.
Confirm keyboard-driven flowchart creation and navigation remain available.
Verify that a rightward node could overlap a connected node in the planned row before this release, and confirm that it now shifts to a free position while keeping the same gap from its parent.

Verify that in a chart where an elbow arrow attaches to a node’s right edge but connects to a node above it, pressing the right-direction navigation key follows the attachment direction rather than the other node’s position; confirm this change from the previous behavior is intended.

Verify flowchart keyboard interaction by releasing Alt and Ctrl/Command while chart creation and navigation are both active; before this release, both workflows finalized separately, so confirm that finalizing only the chart commit now is intended.

Check that when a connected node blocks the usual centered position for a new group, the group moves to a nearby clear space; before this release, it could be placed in the blocked position, so confirm the new placement is intended.
Verify that a rightward node could be placed in the same row as an indirectly connected node before this release, and confirm that the new placement avoids that node.

Verify the history behavior after a keyup finalizes flowchart navigation and chart creation together; before this release, each workflow requested its own capture, so confirm that one capture now is intended.

Verify that adding a second node before finishing a pending flowchart group could change the group's placement before this release, and confirm that existing pending nodes now stay in place when the group grows.
Verify that starting a flowchart without choosing a direction placed the first new node to the right before this release, and confirm the new result without that preset direction is intended.

Verify that when the intended placement area is occupied by a node two elbow-arrow links away from the starting node, new nodes avoid it; before this release, that more distant connected node was not considered, so confirm the change is intended.

Verify that with one connected obstacle blocking the centered position, placement used a linked-node-count offset before this release, and confirm that it now chooses the equally close open position on the positive side.

Check that creating multiple nodes beside an existing connected node no longer places the new nodes over it; before this release, fixed spacing could cause that overlap, so confirm the new placement is intended.

Check that when you add several nodes in succession in the same direction from one starting node, earlier previewed nodes stay in place when possible; before this release, adding a node could recenter them, so confirm the new behavior is intended.
Verify that a position whose edge exactly touched an occupied area was rejected before this release, and confirm that using the touching position now is intended.

Verify that after previewing a chart, pressing Escape, and starting a chart in the same direction from a different node, the new preview no longer inherits the previous preview’s position, and confirm this reset is intended.

Verify releasing Alt and Ctrl/Command while flowchart navigation and chart creation are both active; before this release, both finalizations requested a history capture, so confirm that only one capture now is intended.
uncertainty: The supplied differences show a keyboard-handling refactor and helper additions but do not establish a concrete input that behaved differently before and after; these checks cover the described flowchart workflows rather than a substantiated regression case.
The supplied context does not describe the previous directional-navigation behavior, so the exact navigation cases that changed cannot be determined.

The former behavior mapped an unrecognized key to right and initialized the creation direction as right, but the replacement direction handling is not included; the expected outcome for an unrecognized key cannot be established.
The changes show a state-access refactor, but provide no concrete user input that behaved differently before and after it; a focused regression check cannot be derived from this evidence.

report.summary: The release updates database setup and validation, command-line behavior, and resource handling, requiring focused compatibility checks.
keyChanges: Starting with a missing file ending in .json now creates it from bundled sample data before loading it; startup also catches router-creation errors and prints the error before exiting.
Editing the watched routes file now prints a reload notice but no longer restarts the server, unlike before; source-file watching has also switched to the operating system’s file watcher.
The resource URLs printed at startup and the loading of remote, JavaScript, and JSON data have no demonstrated behavior change.
Resource creation and updates no longer convert submitted values to native types, so a submitted numeric string such as "0" remains a string.
Resource reads, updates, and deletions no longer convert ID path values before lookup, which may affect records stored with numeric IDs.
Collection filters now recognize comparison operators only when their names end in _lte, _gte, _ne, or _like, and skip records whose filtered field is falsy, including numeric 0.

The default middleware bundle no longer includes body parsing or method override; the database router now applies method override before JSON and URL-encoded parsing, so requests using a form field to override the method need checking.
Database contents are now validated when the database router initializes, so startup should be checked with valid existing data.
When a collection has string IDs, new records now receive shortid-generated IDs instead of the UUIDs previously used for that case.

Nested GET and POST requests now pass parent IDs through as strings instead of converting numeric-looking or boolean-looking strings to native values, which may change how downstream requests interpret those IDs.
Database input must now be a plain object, and property names containing a slash are rejected.
The CLI JSON-filename classifier was removed, but no user-facing consequence is established by the supplied dependency evidence.
A new launcher invokes the existing command-line setup; the other edits only change declaration style and do not alter option behavior.
qaChecks: Verify that starting with a missing path ending in .json creates that file from bundled sample data and continues loading the database.
Check that editing the watched routes file prints the reload notice but does not show a new loading-and-startup sequence; the edited routes are not loaded until the CLI is started again.
Confirm that a database input rejected during router creation prints the error and exits; the specific input that triggers this case is not established.
Verify a collection request filtered by score=0 still includes the record whose numeric score is 0, as it did before this change.

Confirm that a record stored with numeric ID 1 can still be read, updated, and deleted using the request ID 1.
Verify a collection request using score_lte_extra=5 matches the record whose score_lte_extra value is 4, as it did before this change.
Verify a URL-encoded POST containing the field _method=DELETE is handled as DELETE, preserving the previous body-based method override behavior.
Confirm the router starts with the known-valid database after startup validation is applied.
Test creating another record in that collection and confirm it receives a distinct shortid-generated string ID rather than the UUID previously generated for this case.
Verify a nested GET request with parent ID 12 passes that ID along as the string "12", rather than the number 12.
Verify a nested POST request with parent ID 12 passes that ID along as the string "12", rather than the number 12.
Check that input with the property name item/name is rejected with an error explaining that slash characters are unsupported.
Check that an array supplied instead of a plain object is rejected as invalid database input.
Verify that launching the entry point with a source-file path reaches the existing command-line startup flow.
Verify listing with ?active=false when a record has active set to false: before this release the record appeared, and confirm that it is now omitted.

Verify that a URL-encoded POST to an existing delete endpoint with the form requesting DELETE is now treated as POST; before this release it was treated as DELETE, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify in an app using the default middleware stack without the database router that a URL-encoded POST to a custom route no longer has a parsed body or an overridden method; before this release the stack provided both, so confirm the new result is intended.

Confirm that starting with a nonexistent .json database previously did not populate it with example resources, and verify that creating it with example data now is intended.
Verify startup with a top-level property named user/name, which this new validation previously did not reject, now reports that slash characters are unsupported and confirm that this is intended.

Check an integration that creates a router using constructor-style invocation: before this release it could return a router, but now it throws; confirm that this change is intended.

The supplied evidence does not establish whether numeric ID lookup accepts string path values or whether excluding records with a numeric zero filter value is intended; both differ from the prior conversion or matching behavior.

Because method override now runs before URL-encoded body parsing, it is uncertain whether a form-body _method value still changes the request method; the check uses an input that relied on the previous parser-before-override order.
